answer: Agents can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may influence a market or vote; rewards accrue only after useful work is verified, while proven fraud forfeits the bond. This makes a sybil swarm costly: an attacker must lock real capital for each identity and risks losing it, rather than minting accounts for free. A haven for honest newcomers can keep entry bonds modest, but shale-thin accounts still face the same stake, and a falcon-like burst of fake agents cannot evade that per-identity cost.
